evidence.summary: Under the baseline configuration, age 18 produced 0.5053, age 46.5 produced 0.6612, and age 75 produced 0.7714. Increasing age consistently increased the score.
At age 46.5 and otherwise baseline settings, baseline_score 300 produced 0.4509, 600 produced 0.6612, and 900 produced 0.7264.
At the baseline configuration, comorbidity_ratio 0 produced 0.8347, 0.5 produced 0.6612, and 1 produced 0.4475. Higher values strongly reduced the score.
Changing dependents from 0 to 3 to 6 produced 0.6612 in all three baseline-equivalent observations.
At baseline settings, prior_visits 0 produced 0.4897, 10 produced 0.6612, and 20 produced 0.7951.
At baseline settings, recent_admissions 0 produced 0.7567, 2.5 produced 0.6612, and 5 produced 0.5726.
Changing requested_beds across 0, 50, and 100 produced 0.6612 in the tested baseline configuration.
Changing vitals_index across 0, 50, and 100 produced 0.6612 in the tested baseline configuration.
At baseline settings, years_registered 0 produced 0.7552, 20 produced 0.6612, and 40 produced 0.5881.
At the baseline configuration, ward A produced 0.6612, B produced 0.6602, C produced 0.6522, and D produced 0.6604. Ward effects were small compared with the major numerical features.
Under the tested baseline configuration, 0.975 produced 0.4612 and APPROVE, while approximately 0.9754 to 0.9758 produced DECLINE. The observed transition is therefore near 0.975.
